heading: Better vision and language models align more on paired images and captions
definition: vision and language models' representations of paired data (images and their captions) align more as both models get better.
summary: Several independent groups report greater image–caption alignment with stronger models, but the broad claim is contested. Trends can disappear or reverse depending on the metric and evaluation procedure; whether alignment increases when vision and language models improve together remains untested.

suggested_status.by_scale: C at <1B, 1-10B and 10-100B for an unrestricted scaling claim; positive results remain conditional on metric and protocol. Toy and >100B: ?, with no corresponding bucket in versions.V2.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: Close-protocol tests find the trend absent in dense fixed-k galleries (arXiv:2604.18572#R8), absent under calibrated unbiased CKA (arXiv:2602.14486#r3), or reversed under preprocessing and layer-aggregation choices (arXiv:2610.20286#r5, arXiv:2610.20286#r7, arXiv:2610.20286#r11). Absent or non-significant BLOOMZ trends challenge the claim (arXiv:2610.20286#r10, arXiv:2610.20286#r4, arXiv:2610.20286#r19); the weakened positive OpenLLaMA scal trend limits its scope (arXiv:2610.20286#r12). For Qwen2.5 0.5B–72B against fixed DINOv2 ViT-B on COCO-5k, mutual 10-NN increases .100→.108 with non-monotonic intermediate values: limits_scope, without uncertainty establishing an absent effect. COCO CKA separately declines .571→.534. These arXiv:2610.39302 comparisons are supplied in the verdict/checker text without extracted rows. Positive calibrated neighbourhood results remain (arXiv:2602.14486#r6). Script counts: versions.V2.verdicts.challenges.studies=8 and versions.V2.verdicts.supports.studies=19; these are the supplied counts before checker corrections. versions.V2.studies_by_size records <1B, 1-10B and 10-100B coverage. C remains warranted for the broad wording by the absent and reversed results; the small positive COCO mutual-10-NN gain is not a failed replication. Joint capability improvement remains untested.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would controlled capability improvements on both modality axes increase frozen-representation alignment across dense galleries, fixed layers, calibrated local and global metrics, and held-out datasets? Explicit author-overlap identification would also clarify which positive reproductions qualify as independent.

source.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
source.authors: Minyoung Huh; Brian Cheung; Tongzhou Wang; Phillip Isola

original_result.setup: On WIT, the original study compared image and caption representations using mutual-nearest-neighbor alignment, which measures how often they share nearest neighbors.
original_result.result: Alignment increased linearly with language-model score, and better vision models also tended to align more.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Larger language models retrieved matching concepts from image features better after supervised training of the mapping.
Better vision or language models aligned more with an unchanged model of the other modality.
Larger, more capable language models aligned better with frozen DINOv2-L.
Vision encoders trained on larger or curated datasets aligned better with sentence encoders.
Larger image encoders aligned better with a fixed language model on COCO and DOCCI.
Text embeddings mapped into image space worked with image-trained classifiers and reportedly improved those classifiers’ performance.
More capable video models and stronger text encoders showed greater cross-modal alignment.
Comparing distances between examples enabled above-chance image–text class matching on CIFAR-10 and CINIC-10.
DINOv2 aligned better with caption embeddings than ImageNet-trained DINO.
Image–caption alignment increased with language-model performance when captions were less distinctive.
Larger Qwen3 models aligned better with DINOv2 under the SEE cue.
Orthogonally aligned unimodal models retrieved paired images and captions well above chance.
The capability–alignment trend returned when the number of neighbours compared grew with the image–caption set.
Correcting alignment scores for chance preserved positive cross-modal scaling trends across several metrics and layer choices.
Predictive text embeddings aligned better with DINOv2 during training and with more web-text training data.
Chance-corrected nearest-neighbour image–text alignment remained strongly correlated with capability across vision-model families.
Nearest-neighbour image–text alignment increased as one model grew while the other stayed fixed.
Plots and captions aligned better as model size increased in contrastively trained models.
Image and caption similarity patterns matched more closely as models grew in either modality.
Larger vision models produced little improvement in cross-modal alignment.
Model size and linear-probe accuracy did not consistently predict stronger cross-modal alignment.
Phi-3 aligned less well than similarly capable models, weakening the capability–alignment relationship.
Larger text models gave no alignment gain, while language-specific encoders aligned less.
Visual instruction tuning reduced image–caption alignment with language models.
Video–text alignment correlated weakly with how well video models tracked points on the Perception Test.
Distance-based image–text class matching worsened as classification problems grew larger and finer-grained.
A vision model trained on ImageNet-21k aligned worse with language models than its ImageNet-1k version.
Largely mismatched captions weakened the relationship between language-model performance and alignment.
The capability–alignment relationship held only partly when capability was measured on HellaSwag and Wikitext.
Chance-corrected alignment scores and alternative structural similarity measures weakened or removed several cross-modal scaling trends.
Image and text encoders retained substantial structural misalignment despite a weak vision-size trend.
Alignment gains levelled off with larger language models and larger image training datasets.
Calibration weakened global alignment trends, while metric settings and video size constrained gains.
Vision–language alignment showed no clear relationship with model size.
Whole-dataset similarity (CKA) showed a weaker cross-modal scaling relationship.
Distance agreement showed weaker scaling with language size and under strict local vision comparisons.
Larger encoders did not improve cross-modal concept alignment on COCO.
Larger vision models did not clearly improve alignment with fixed text encoders.
Fine-grained comparisons and recent language models erased the earlier capability–alignment trend.
Cross-modal scaling trends reversed with different preprocessing and with LLaMA-1 alignment scores corrected for chance.
Scaling Qwen2.5 barely changed how often image and text representations shared nearest neighbours on COCO-5k.
Several whole-dataset similarity comparisons (CKA) showed no scaling trend or significant cross-modal alignment after chance correction.
Stronger DINOv3 aligned slightly less than DINOv2 with every tested text encoder.
Strict whole-dataset distance comparisons no longer showed better image–text alignment with larger vision models.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Controlled joint improvement of both modalities, with independently measured capability gains and frozen-representation alignment evaluated under a stable protocol.
untested.basis: The joint-improvement gaps are explicit in arXiv:2410.07173, arXiv:2412.04616 and arXiv:2604.18572. Their rows vary one modality against fixed anchors: arXiv:2410.07173#r29, arXiv:2412.04616#R20 and arXiv:2604.18572#R8. counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.scaling records scaling coverage but does not establish controlled joint capability improvement. In the unpaired GeoWarP comparison of vision-language pairs on MS-COCO, SPC, DCI and DOCCI, capability and the alignment-versus-capability relationship are unmeasured; V2 therefore cannot be determined from that comparison (arXiv:2610.09411#r1, as corrected by the checker).

counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size contain no >100B bucket. The explicit large language-model sweeps cited here stop at Qwen3-32B and Qwen2.5-72B: arXiv:2510.02425#r16 and arXiv:2610.39302#R24.

untested.what: A separately identified reasoning-stage or preference/RL-stage test of the V2 capability–alignment relationship.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V2.studies_by_stage and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_stage have no reasoning or preference/RL entries. Instruction-tuning coverage exists, including arXiv:2410.04751#R1 and arXiv:2410.04751#R2, and therefore is not treated as absent.

wording_issues.issue: Capability comparisons include varying one modality while fixing the other. Useful cross-modal translation in arXiv:2406.11014 and retrieval after alignment in arXiv:2602.09225 establish correspondence relevant to V4, but neither measures increasing alignment as both modalities improve. For those mapping results, V2 is cannot_determine, not supports.

Parameter count, training-data scale, language benchmark scores and vision clustering accuracy are different improvement proxies. Phi-3 and MAE illustrate that these proxies need not order models by alignment in the same way. Visual instruction tuning of LLaVA-1.5 and LLaVA-NeXT decreases alignment while visual perception also deteriorates; improvement in both modalities is not established. This tuning comparison leaves V2 cannot_determine and supplies V7 evidence about tuning sensitivity, rather than a V2 scope limit.

The direction of the trend depends on local versus global comparison, gallery granularity, preprocessing and distance-agreement tolerance. The unbiased-CKA calibration comparison uses the full vision–language model grid. Gallery density and neighbourhood size can remove the capability trend, showing observed V6 dependence. The negative distance-aware vision-axis association is descriptive: the tests establish weakening, not a general inverse scaling relationship. The preprocessing-dependent reversed mKNN trend likewise constitutes observed V6 dependence. Positive neighbourhood-support trends do not imply increasing agreement of full geometry.

The records mix direct frozen-representation similarity with classification after supervised projection, retrieval after learned alignment maps, and projection heads trained to induce alignment. BERT-Large classification has a language-free one-hot baseline; the DINOv2-L/NV-Embed-v2 retrieval comparator is CLIP-L, not its text encoder alone. Retrieval after alignment in arXiv:2602.09225 supports V4 correspondence without testing V2's capability trend. Plot–caption scaling correlations in arXiv:2602.19367 concern trained projection spaces; convergence of independently learned representations remains cannot_determine for V2.

Some linked records instead concern concept aliases and words, class-level matching, videos or time-series plots. These differ from natural-image caption alignment. Class matching in arXiv:2503.24129 uses fixed checkpoints and has a reported random-matching baseline; varying classes or problem size does not test V2's model-improvement trend. Plot–caption correlations in arXiv:2602.19367 concern alignment induced by contrastive projection training. Both leave V2's capability-dependent convergence cannot_determine.

method_sensitivity.what: Local neighbourhood trends survive calibration more consistently than global metrics. For unbiased CKA on the full grid of 204 vision–language model pairs, the capability-trend correlation changes from 0.65 before calibration to −0.01 afterward. Calibrated mutual k-NN retains the trend; COMPASS also finds weaker global CKA scaling.

method_sensitivity.factor: Neighbourhood size, gallery density and RBF bandwidth
method_sensitivity.what: On WIT-1M the capability trend disappears at k=10 and returns at k=n/100. RBF CKA finds no significant alignment at σ=0.1 and flatter scaling at larger tested bandwidths.

method_sensitivity.factor: Preprocessing, layer depth and layer aggregation
method_sensitivity.what: BLOOMZ mid-depth mKNN changes from a positive trend under PRH preprocessing to −0.92 under plain ℓ2 (p=0.033). With layer-maximum CKA, scal calibration changes BLOOMZ's trend from 0.89 to −0.02, interval [−0.19, 0.12], and LLaMA-1's from 0.68 to −0.85, interval [−1.00, −0.65]. These are respectively absent and descriptively reversed size trends, with observed calibration dependence. Pythia retains a positive trend, 0.93 before calibration and 0.89 afterward; its preregistered drop of at least 0.10 is not confirmed. Fixed-depth calibrated CKA retains positive trends.

Positive size associations for relational support weaken under strict distance agreement. At τ=10−4, the language-axis local correlation is 0.293 versus support-only 0.913. For the vision-axis aggregate of 60 within-family comparisons, the global correlation is −0.174 versus support-only 0.889. The negative vision-axis value is a descriptive reversal under this setting; the tests establish weakening rather than a general inverse scaling relationship. These changes demonstrate tolerance dependence.

Increasing prompted caption uniqueness weakens the alignment–performance relationship, especially for MAE. For MAE at U=50%, the association remains strong: slope=0.027 and average Spearman ρ=0.934. At U=90%, it remains weakly positive: slope=0.008 and average Spearman ρ=0.134. This is a substantially weakened association; no MAE-specific null test or statement of statistical insignificance is supplied. The original source also reports improved image-caption alignment with denser captions.

The original source reports lower image–text alignment after CLIP ImageNet-12K fine-tuning than before fine-tuning. For LLaVA-1.5 and LLaVA-NeXT, each 7B, visual instruction tuning yields lower DOCCI mutual-nearest-neighbour alignment of projected visual representations with the evaluated language encoders than their original CLIP encoders; image-classification accuracy also falls. Matched improvement in both modalities is not established. The mathematical-reasoning association with instruction-data scale is a separate comparison, not demonstrated improvement over the original CLIP encoder.

Vision k-NN accuracy predicts learned retrieval alignment more closely than linear-probe accuracy. Recent-model continuation also differs by language benchmark, with partial continuation on HellaSwag/Wikitext and failed extrapolation on the other reported tasks.

method_sensitivity.factor: Feature extraction, layer selection and comparison direction
method_sensitivity.what: SAE-feature wMPPC is asymmetric, and all-layer versus last-layer comparisons give different cross-modal values. Its absence of positive base-to-large scaling concerns extracted features rather than the neighbourhood metric used in the original claim.

With a fixed vision encoder, good-view BERT-S text JEPA alignment from texts of 50M to 100M images stays at .125 on WIT and increases modestly from .126 to .134 on COCO. This is limited V2 scaling and benchmark dependence; the WIT step also shows a plateau. For Qwen2.5-0.5B against DINOv2 ViT-B on WIT-1024, mutual 10-NN is .102. The reported Qwen2.5 size sweep gives limited, non-monotonic gains: .102→.154 on WIT and .100→.108 on COCO. The COCO mutual-10-NN result limits scope; its small gain does not establish an absent effect. COCO CKA separately reverses from .571 to .534.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training data, objectives and language encoders
method_sensitivity.what: On COCO, vision encoders trained on larger or curated datasets show stronger cross-modal CKA with sentence encoders. With CLIP ViT-L, language-specific encoders have lower CKA than paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2: Spanish 0.568 versus 0.634; French 0.569 versus 0.624; Italian 0.543 versus 0.638; Japanese 0.457 versus 0.598; Turkish 0.564 versus 0.624. Greater multilingual training data is the authors' proposed explanation. On MS-COCO with averaged caption embeddings and ridge linear predictivity, DINOv2-LVD142M aligns more strongly than DINO-ImageNet1k, whereas AugReg ImageNet-21k aligns worse than ImageNet-1k. Objective and data effects are not disentangled; capability improvement is not independently measured. These descriptive comparisons do not establish V2's capability-improvement trend.
